question_stem:
A U-tube contains liquid, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:figure_4_1}}

{{figure:figure_4_2}}

The total length of the liquid column is $L$.

The column of liquid is displaced so that the change in height of the liquid level from the equilibrium position in each arm of the U-tube is $x$, as shown in Fig. 4.2.

The liquid in the U-tube then oscillates such that its acceleration $a$ is given by the expression

$$a = -\left(\frac{2g}{L}\right)x$$

where $g$ is the acceleration of free fall.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the liquid column undergoes simple harmonic motion.

parts.label: (b)
(c)(i)
parts.part_stem: The oscillations shown in Fig. 4.3 are damped.
parts.text: Suggest one cause of this damping.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the ratio

$$\frac{\text{total energy of oscillations after 1.5 complete oscillations}}{\text{total initial energy of oscillations}}$$
